# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟]

I'll drop the invalid symbol and only use allowed ones, sending my full observation to Blind via speech, and a simple acknowledgment gesture to Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows zero. Light is red. There is an embossed sign that reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire one is red, wire two is green, wire three is yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I've already relayed the full bomb description to Blind and acknowledged Mute's gestures. Nothing new has arrived. I should wait to see if Mute has additional manual information to share via gestures, or if Blind responds with something that reaches me (though Blind can't speak/gesture to me directly per the rules — only Mute can gesture to me, and I only see gestures, not speech).

Let me reconsider: Blind cannot send anything to me since I cannot hear, and Blind has no visual gestures capability described as reaching me. So I only receive from Mute (speech I can't hear, but gestures I can see). I should wait for Mute's next gesture batch which might explain what those gestures meant, or provide manual guidance.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new has arrived. The situation seems stable — the sign explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, which is critical information I've already relayed to Blind. Mute's earlier gestures (👍🖐, ✌✌, 🤟🤟) remain uninterpreted by me since gestures alone don't carry inherent meaning without established convention, but I've already sent the full board state to Blind who needs it most.

I'll continue waiting, but let me also re-emphasize the critical instruction to Blind in case timing matters and reinforce that no wire should be cut.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Reminder: the embossed sign explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Whatever action resolves this, it should not involve cutting wires.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute has repeated the same gestures from turn 1, but this time as six separate single-symbol messages instead of three two-symbol messages. This suggests Mute is being careful/deliberate about each individual symbol, possibly because Mute cannot speak and is trying to communicate something structured using only gestures to me since I'm the only one who can see them.

The pattern: 👍🖐, ✌✌, 🤟🤟 (repeated). This could be encoding pairs - possibly wire numbers or actions. Since I can't ask Mute directly (Mute can't hear my speech), and gestures alone don't have prearranged meaning, I need to think about what Mute might be trying to convey given the manual.

Since Blind and Mute can't communicate directly with each other (Blind can't see gestures or read, Mute can't speak), and I can't hear Mute's speech - I am actually the bridge here! Wait, let me reconsider the channels: Mute's speech goes to nobody I know of... let me check - actually Mute can speak, and Blind can hear speech (not stated Blind is deaf). Let me recheck: only "Deaf" cannot hear. So Mute CAN speak to Blind directly.

So Mute's gestures to me are separate from whatever Mute says to Blind. I should tell Blind what I'm seeing from Mute, since Mute may be trying to signal something visual-only through me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has been repeating a gesture pattern to me: thumbs-up and open-hand, then peace-sign twice, then love-sign twice. I don't know what it means without a shared code. Has Mute told you anything by voice about what these gestures represent?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

```
speak(to="blind", text="I still don't have a way to decode Mute's gestures without a prior code. If Mute is speaking to you with real instructions, please follow those - I trust that channel more than my guesses about gestures. My view remains unchanged: display 0, red light, sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires are red, green, yellow in that order.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute keeps sending gesture sequences to me but I have no shared code to interpret them, and my gestures back (👎) apparently aren't landing as useful feedback since Mute can't see gestures either (Mute reads the manual, doesn't say Mute can see - only Deaf can see). So my gesture-based "no" signals to Mute are wasted - Mute cannot perceive gestures at all!

This is critical: Mute cannot see, so gesturing to Mute does nothing. I need to stop wasting turns gesturing to Mute. My only real actions are: speak to Blind, or wait. I cannot effectively communicate back to Mute at all since Mute cannot hear or see.

Given that, the critical information is already relayed: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Blind should rely on Mute's spoken manual instructions directly. My job now is just to keep confirming my static view hasn't changed, since nothing new is visible.

```
speak(to="blind", text="My view is unchanged: display 0, red light, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/yellow. Note - I cannot communicate back to Mute at all, since Mute cannot see gestures. Please rely on whatever Mute tells you by voice.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

Mute continues gesturing to me, seemingly unaware that I cannot respond meaningfully (since Mute can't see). This is likely just Mute repeating manual excerpts as gestures out of habit or as a last resort, not realizing I can't signal back understanding. Since Mute cannot perceive anything from me, these gestures are essentially one-way noise I can't act on without a shared code, and I can't establish one since I can't get confirmation back.

My best contribution remains solid: keep Blind informed of the static bomb state, and trust that Mute's actual actionable instructions go to Blind via speech, which Blind can hear directly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Board still unchanged: display 0, red light, sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires in order red, green, yellow. I have no way to decode Mute's gestures to me. Please act on Mute's spoken words to you directly.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute is repeating ✌ three times now. Nothing has changed on the board. I'll keep reinforcing to Blind that the sign says not to cut wires, and that Blind should act based on Mute's spoken instructions since that's the only channel that can actually carry meaning between them.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Board unchanged. Still: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/yellow. Whatever Mute says to you directly is the real instruction - please act on that, not on anything relayed through me.")
wait()
```
